#4462. Hyundai claims 2027’s ‘Best EV Brand’ title as the IONIQ 5 and IONIQ 9 impress

Hyundai’s electric SUVs are getting some love. The IONIQ 5 and three-row IONIQ 9 helped the Korean automaker land its first-ever “Best Electric Vehicle Brand” award from US News & World Report for 2027.

“This win showcases the breadth and strength of Hyundai’s SUV and electric lineups,” Alex Kwanten, managing editor at Autos at US News, said after naming it the Best EV Brand and Best SUV Brand for 2027.

This marks the first time Hyundai has earned the Best EV Brand award and the third consecutive win for Best SUV Brand.

Including hybrid and electric vehicles, Hyundai offers ten unique SUVs, “many of them at or near the top of our rankings in those classes for capability, comfort, performance and value,” Kwanten said.

Hyundai’s fully electric SUVs, the IONIQ 5 and IONIQ 9, “in particular, stand out for their combination of style and technology,” he explained.

Hyundai currently offers the IONIQ 5, including the sporty IONIQ 5 N and off-road-focused IONIQ 5 XRT, plus the three-row IONIQ 9.

Although Hyundai discontinued its electric sedan, the IONIQ 6, after the 2025 model year, the new high-performance IONIQ 6 N joins the lineup in 2027.

The IONIQ 5 continued to earn praise, taking its third consecutive Best Compact Electric SUV award. Its larger sibling, the IONIQ 9, took the top spot in the midsize electric SUV category.

Hyundai’s IONIQ 5 is the most popular EV in the US this year through September that isn’t a Tesla, ranking third behind the Model Y and Model 3.

Why does it continue winning over buyers? The IONIQ 5 checks all the boxes with long-range capabilities, fast charging, and a surprisingly spacious interior with modern tech.

It’s also among the most affordable EVs in the US. Prices for the 2027 Hyundai IONIQ 5 start at just $35,250.

However, the base price is for the standard-range IONIQ 5 SE with an EPA-estimated range of up to 245 miles. Upgrading to the extended-range SE RWD model costs an extra $2,500, with prices starting at $37,750, but it offers up to 318 miles of range.

The three-row Hyundai IONIQ 9 electric SUV starts at $58,955 with an EPA-estimated range of up to 335 miles.

Hyundai’s IONIQ 5 is about the size of a Tesla Model Y, with two rows of seating and space for five passengers. Hyundai’s larger IONIQ 9 offers three rows of seating with six- or seven-seat options.

The larger IONIQ 9 offers up to 163.54 cubic feet of interior passenger volume, compared with up to 106.5 cubic feet in the IONIQ 5.

Both electric SUVs use an 800-volt electrical architecture for ultra-fast charging. The IONIQ 5 can charge from 10% to 80% in about 20 minutes, while the IONIQ 9 takes around 24 minutes using a 350 kW DC fast charger.

Hyundai assembles the IONIQ 5 and IONIQ 9 at the Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America outside of Savannah, Georgia.

When we toured the facility earlier this year, Hyundai told Electrek that its electric SUVs are winning over new buyers at a higher rate than any of its gas or hybrid vehicles.

The IONIQ 5 had a 69.8% conquest rate last year, while the IONIQ 9 had 64.3%. Hyundai’s Elantra N ranked third (61.9%), followed by the Palisade (61.2%) and Kona Electric (60.9%).

#4461. Aptera Finally Built Its First Car For Customer Delivery

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Excuse me while I go find a hat to eat, because Aptera just sold and delivered its first production car. Nothing against Aptera specifically, but when a company hangs around for 20 years, while exchanging ownership hands several times without actually producing anything for customers, I start to get skeptical. However, Aptera Motors just did what so many doubters thought it'd never do: It delivered a road-legal production vehicle to one of its first early investors.

Aptera calls its early investors "Accelerators," and Accelerator #1 was Martin Hartono, CEO of the Indonesia-based GDP Ventures. While Hartono wasn't on site in Carslbad, California to take delivery of the very first Aptera, a representative from GDP Ventures was there in his place. The matte black "Noir" model will soon be exported for Hartono and it will live outside of the U.S.

“This is the moment our team has worked toward for years,” said Chris Anthony, Co-CEO of Aptera. “To Accelerator #1, and to every reservation holder and shareholder who believed in this vehicle: thank you. We’re working to complete more vehicles for early customers as soon as possible.”

“What excites me about Aptera is how innovation can redefine the way we use energy in everyday mobility. By combining solar technology, battery power and an ultra-efficient vehicle design, Aptera offers a compelling solution for people who want to minimize their energy consumption without compromising the ability to travel long distances. As an early believer in Aptera, I am proud to be part of this milestone and to see this vision become a reality,” said Martin Hartono, CEO of GDP Venture.

Aptera's hook is that its three-wheeled EVs come with solar roofs designed to harness enough sunlight to add up to 40 miles of range per day. While that won't always be the case, Aptera proved, with third-party verification, that its cars are actually capable of exceeding that in the right conditions. Will that revolutionize electric motoring the way Aptera hopes to? That's yet to be seen, but it does offer a interesting concept for customers who don't have long commutes and leave their car parked outside for most of the day while they work. In addition to plugging in to recharge, doesn't it sound nice to recoup your morning commute mileage with the sun while you're in the office?

Whether this three-wheeled rolling solar panel ends up being a hit or not, and whether Aptera can stick around long enough to become a successful automaker, will take much longer to learn. But actually delivering a production car is a good place to start. Even if Aptera couldn't beat GTA 6 to launch.

#4460. 2027 Lamborghini Temerario

See all results for new 2027 Lamborghini Temerario for sale near 14202

The Temerario might be the runt of the Lamborghini supercar litter, but it's still one raging bull. Taking the reins from its widely lauded Huracan predecessor, the Temerario is the least expensive way into Lambo's supercar lineup, but it doesn’t sacrifice much performance compared to the company's Revuelto flagship—in fact, it beats its brawnier older brother to 60 mph by a tenth of a second.

Under the Temerario's origami-folded sheetmetal lies a newly developed 4.0-liter twin-turbo V-8 nestled into the car's aluminum spaceframe just ahead of the rear axle. As if 789 horsepower from the engine alone wasn’t enough, a trio of electric motors—one mounted between the engine and transmission and one at each front wheel—ups its total output to 907 Italian stallions. If you somehow tire of the sound of the flat-plane-crank V-8's goosebump-raising 10,000-rpm wail, the electric motors also allow for short periods of silent, all-electric driving. With its mighty hybrid-assisted thrust, poster-worthy looks, and agile moves, the Temerario is every inch a purebred Lambo and well worthy of supercar status.

Expert Tip: If you'd rather have a horse instead of a bull in your garage, the Ferrari 296GTB is a steed with the need for speed, and moves to match the Lambo for a similar price.

Compare the 2027 Lamborghini Temerario with the top vehicles in this segment with our new compare tool.

A droptop Temerario Spyder is new for 2027, and it features a retractable hardtop that folds in 17 seconds at speeds up to 31 mph.

If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.

The Temerario's powertrain consists of a twin-turbo 4.0-liter V-8 with a flat-plane crankshaft, a trio of axial-flux electric motors, and an eight-speed dual-clutch transmission. The Temerario's V-8 alone is good for 789 horsepower; adding the output of the three electric motors brings the total combined output to 907 horsepower. That's just 94 ponies shy of the Lamborghini Revuelto, the brand's V-12 halo car. On the Temerario, one electric motor mounts to the V-8 in front of the transmission, while the remaining two live up front, one at each wheel. The Temerario's V-8 redlines at 10,000 rpm, and the engine's peak torque of 538 pound-feet is available from 4000 to 7000 rpm. While the flat-plane-crank V-8 sounds glorious when pushed to its limit, we wish that its exhaust packed a bit more fury earlier in the rev range.

With the electric motors in play, maximum torque output rises to 590 pound-feet. In addition to supplying enormous power, the hybrid configuration helps provide instantaneous torque and linear power delivery over a broad range of speeds and driving situations. Thirteen drive programs are available via a rotary button on the steering wheel, including launch and drift modes, the latter offering three levels of tail-out leeway. We drove the Temerario at the track and on the street and were enthralled with its lively powertrain and playful demeanor.

Car and Driver calculates your car's value in three free and easy steps - using the same Black Book® data dealers use to appraise vehicles.

In Comparison: In our testing, the Temerario got to 60 mph in a ridiculously quick 2.1 seconds. It also ripped through the quarter-mile in 9.4 seconds at 150 miles per hour. Both figures beat its big sibling, the Revuelto, by 0.3 seconds and 2 mph, respectively.

Juice is stored in a 3.8-kWh lithium-ion battery pack. The battery resides in the center tunnel along with the transmission—the location is said to help optimize weight distribution and is protected from underneath by structural elements. Regenerative braking and power from the internal-combustion engine both replenish the battery's state of charge. Plug-in charging is also possible via a standard 7-kW onboard charger; with typical household current, it can recharge an empty battery to full capacity in a claimed 30 minutes. An EV-only mode provides around 4 miles of range.

The EPA estimates that the Temerario will deliver 14 mpg city, 19 mpg highway, and 16 mpg combined. When we get a chance to test the Temerario, we'll update this story with results from our 75-mph highway fuel economy test. For more information about the Temerario's fuel economy, visit the EPA's website.

First Row: Thanks to its all-aluminum chassis, the Temerario's interior offers more space than the Huracán it replaced. Headroom increased by 1.3 inches, legroom by 1.8 inches, and Lamborghini claims the interior is large enough to accommodate drivers up to six feet five wearing a helmet. The interior shares some styling cues from the Revuelto; four stitching patterns are available, and the 18-way adjustable driver's seat is heated and ventilated. The Temerario also borrows the Revuelto's steering wheel, which is too busy with controls for our liking.

Cargo Capacity: If you're planning on taking the Temerario on a weekend getaway, you'd better pack light; the front trunk only has a four-cubic-foot capacity.

Lamborghini says the Temerario offers the most advanced suite of infotainment and connectivity features of any model in its lineup. Three displays—a 12.3-inch instrument panel with three user-selectable views, an 8.4-inch infotainment screen, and a 9.1-inch passenger screen—occupy prime dashboard real estate. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard, as is a Sonus Faber audio system.

The most notable feature, though, is the optional Lamborghini Vision Unit (LAVU) system. Essentially an on-board data acquisition system, the setup utilizes three cameras: one viewing the road, one focused on the passengers, and one looking forward over the driver's shoulder. Preloaded with data for 150 different racing circuits, the system can be used to evaluate and improve driver performance. It also enables a "memories recorder" function that allows for up to two minutes of off-track recording, and works as a dashcam that can capture one minute of incident history.

Compared to most other cars, the Temerario doesn't offer many driver-assistance features.

For information about the Temerario's crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.

Compared with most mainstream automakers, Lamborghini doesn't provide stellar warranty coverage. But its protection plans are competitive with those of high-end rivals such as Ferrari and can be enhanced by optional extended coverage. A five-year complimentary scheduled maintenance plan is now standard.

Each year, we put hundreds of vehicles through our rigorous instrumented testing regimen. If the data in the chart below is for a different model year, that's because this vehicle hasn't changed from when we last tested it, and the test results remain accurate.

#4458. It’s official: Battlefield 6 is 2025's best-selling game, but Black Ops 7 still managed to be November’s top-seller

2025 will be remembered for many things, but in the ultra-competitive games industry, it’s going to be thought of as the year Battlefield 6 did what many thought couldn’t happen.

Circan’s November 2025 video game sales report has easily been one of the most anticipated. For one, November is always one of the most lucrative for the games industry, but this year in particular has seen several major hits - including new entries in two rival series.

We’re talking, of course, about Battlefield 6, and Black Ops 7 the latest releases in their respective multiplayer shooter series. The decades-old fight to claim the top spot has long been won by Call of Duty, but the latest Battlefield has achieved what many thought was impossible.

Cricana’s report covers spending on video game software, hardware, and accessories in the U.S. November 2025 saw spending fall by 4% compared to November 2024, bringing in a total of $5.9 billion.

Software technically saw growth during the month, but declines in hardware, and accessories were mainly responsible for the drop in overall spending. Black Ops 7 continued Call of Duty’s 18-Year Streak in topping sales in its launch month.

However, this year’s game did not also top the year-to-date charts, something the series has done consistently, and more than any other top-selling game each year - with rare exceptions. Battlefield 6 is firmly in the lead there, cementing its claim as 2025’s best-selling title. Black Ops 7, fittingly, occupies in the #7 spot there.

Separately from the best-selling game title fight, November has actually been one of the worst for the industry in terms of hardware sales. The report notes that the three major platform holders - Sony, Microsoft, and Nintendo have all seen their hardware sales decline.

Spending on hardware during November amounted to only $695 million, a massive 27% decline compared to November 2024. According to the report, that’s the worst dollar amount total for any November since 2005, when it comes to hardware specifically. All three current-gen consoles totaled 1.6 million units sold, which Circana also notes is the lowest for any November since 1995.

This all doesn’t bode especially well for the industry. November has always been a key holiday shopping month, but it’s clear the constantly rising console prices - and already high game prices - have had a big impact.

#4456. When the Work Gets Heavy, Do Your Tires Hold Up? Cooper’s New Discoverer® HT Is Built to Carry the Weight

Evolved from severe-duty all-terrain designs and backed by an up to 70,000-mile Limited Treadwear Warranty, this highway tire pairs interlocking 3D tread sipes with rigid construction to keep your truck or SUV composed on high-mileage trips.

For enthusiasts, tire shopping is an upgrade, not a chore. While the casual driver might treat new tires like regular maintenance, anyone who cares about vehicle dynamics knows that what meets the road defines how a truck or SUV rides, tracks, and stops. It is the single most transformative upgrade you can make to your vehicle. For more than 110 years, Cooper tires have catered to drivers who look past the showroom floor and seek out products that overdeliver on performance, capability, and long-term durability.

And that level of purpose-built engineering is more vital than ever. As vehicles grow heavier and more capable, tires need to do more than simply roll down an interstate. They have to withstand heavy payload demands, sudden weather changes, and unpredictable pavement. Cooper tires are built to that benchmark. Rooted in American engineering and real-world development, Cooper tires are built to an uncompromising standard that live up to their promises. From the rock-crawling STT Pro to the severe-snow-designated Stronghold AT, the Discoverer® family has earned its reputation through real-world testing from Alaskan ice to jagged mountain trails.

The new Cooper Discoverer® HT adapts that rugged all-terrain lineage for long-distance highway cruising, matching heavy-duty capability with quiet, refined composure. While it retains the structural durability to wander down a gravel trail with a trailer in tow, its core mission is maximizing comfort and control across hundreds of miles of open road.

Where many highway tires trade load capability for a soft ride, the Discoverer® HT is engineered to handle both. Straight, reinforced sidewalls provide the structural foundation needed to maintain an optimal contact patch under load. Whether the vehicle is running light or carrying family, gear, and tongue weight, the tire resists deformation, ensuring consistent steering response and predictable roadholding grip in any condition. It’s engineered for drivers whose tires have to hold their own—providing a dependable, hard-working partner that won’t fold when the truck or SUV is pushed to its limit.

Cooper tires also tackle truck and SUV tire performance, with advanced features. Its proprietary 3-D Micro-Gauge Siping incorporates interlocking zig-zag sipes inside the tread blocks. Under heavy braking, sharp turns, or loaded acceleration, these interlocking sipes lock together to stiffen the tread block, to help support responsiveness. Crucially, these sipes run deep into the tread rubber, ensuring that gripping edges are still present to help with traction. That structural integrity backs up an exceptional UTQG treadwear rating of 720 and a 70,000-mile limited treadwear warranty on passenger fitments.

This is the tire for drivers who expect their trucks or suvs to show up for the long haul. Whether that means towing a camper into the backcountry, handling moving-day payloads, or eating up cross-country interstate miles in quiet comfort, the mission remains the same: a single set of tires that balances real-world traction, refined manners, and hard-working capability.

To fit that wide spectrum of work, Cooper offers the Discoverer® HT across 19 passenger sizes covering 16- to 22-inch wheels (with section widths from 245 to 285 mm), alongside 16 light-truck (LT) options engineered with deeper tread grooves and higher load ratings. Backed by a 45-day satisfaction guarantee and over a century of research and development, the Discoverer® HT delivers what Cooper has always stood for: the quiet confidence that the job was done right.

#4455. Kia’s cheapest EV is coming next year, and it could cost under $25,000

Kia’s EV lineup covers just about every size and price point, but it believes one thing is still missing: a truly cheap electric car. That’s about to change in 2027, when Kia plans to unveil a new EV that could start at around $22,000 to $24,000.

It’s been 40 years since Kia introduced its first electric vehicle, the Besta EV, created so runners in the 1986 Asian Games wouldn’t have to breathe toxic fumes from the broadcast vehicle.

Kia has come a long way since the Besta EV hit the road, now offering a complete lineup of electric vehicles, from compact SUVs and hatchbacks to vans and three-row SUVs.

In Europe and the UK, Kia’s electric lineup consists of the EV2, EV3, EV4, EV5, EV6, EV9, and PV5 van, but the Korean automaker isn’t done yet.

“With no intention of resting on its laurels,” Kia said, the brand plans to complete development of its first software-defined vehicle (SDV) by the end of 2027, an all-new B-segment EV hatchback.

It didn’t offer any other details on the upcoming EV, but Ted Lee, Kia’s executive vice president and head of global operations, told Auto Express that Kia and Hyundai are co-developing a new dedicated EV architecture for an upcoming pair of entry-level electric cars.

Expected to arrive as the Hyundai IONIQ 1 and Kia EV1, the new EVs will compete with other entry-level electric cars like the Renault Twingo, which starts at about €20,000.

Lee said the EV1’s price will be highly competitive not just with other entry-level EVs, but also with small gas-powered cars, with prices expected to start in the €20,000 to €22,000 range, or about $22,000 to $24,000. And that’s without government incentives.

The EV2 starts at just €26,600 ($29,500) in Germany and other European markets as Kia’s current entry-level EV, so the price range would make sense.

While it will be Kia’s cheapest EV, Lee promised it would not cut corners in quality, design, or features.

As its first SDV, the EV1 will feature Kia and Hyundai Motor’s latest-generation tech and software. Kia said the electric SDV will offer Level 2+ autonomous driving on highways. In 2029, Kia plans to expand to Level 2++, enabling it to operate in cities.

The new EV will also use Hyundai’s SDV architecture (CODA), the Pleos Connect infotainment system, and Gleo AI, an in-vehicle Agenic AI.

What will the EV1 look like? According to Auto Express, the entry-level EV will look a bit sportier and less boxy than the EV2 SUV. It could draw inspiration from the Vision Meta Turismo concept.

It also apparently won’t be based on the Picanto, Kia’s smallest gas-powered car. The Kia EV1 is expected to bring a unique style to the family.

This is good to see and makes sense, especially in Europe. I don't think Kia can go wrong making vehicles at so many different price points. It allows them to reach different segments and almost literally have something for almost everyone.

While all of Kia’s current EVs feature its ccNC infotainment system with dual 12.3″ instrument display and infotainment screens, plus a 5″ climate control panel, the EV1 could bring a simpler setup.

Like its other electric models, the EV1 is expected to receive the GT treatment. However, as an entry-level model, it may not use a dual-motor all-wheel-drive setup like the others.

Will Kia bring the EV1 to the US? Don’t get your hopes up. Kia has previously said the B-segment hatchback is designed for Europe. It could even be built alongside the EV2 at Kia’s plant in Slovakia.

The good news? The EV3, Kia’s compact electric SUV, is now on sale in the US, starting at just $29,890.

#4454. The Volkswagen ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Is A Two-Seat Track-Ready EV

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Volkswagen may not be in the best place right now, but that’s not stopping it from spending big money to celebrate the 50th anniversary of the legendary GTI badge. The latest showpiece is the Volkswagen ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept, a one-off electric hatchback built for the track that sheds a set of doors and borrows the electric motor from its bigger brothers.

The striking electric race car comes after the production-ready ID. Polo GTI and the upcoming ID.3 GTI, and its purpose is to show what the German brand can do with its modular MEB+ platform. In fact, Volkswagen is calling itself the “master of modular platforms,” proudly saying that the same architecture that underpins the bog-standard ID. Polo is capable of impressive extremes, from the ultra-efficient Mission Efficiency to the performance-oriented GTI Clubsport EV.

That said, making the latest one-off wasn’t easy. Engineers had to take an APP550 electric motor, which was originally designed for rear-wheel-drive models like the ID.7 and ID. Tiguan, and adapt it for the ID. Polo chassis, which is front-wheel-drive.

To fit the larger drive unit in the small hatchback, the whole front section of the car had to be modified, which meant designing and building an entirely new subframe. The longitudinal chassis members, stabilizer bar, several mounting points, and various chassis components also had to be redesigned to make the taller APP550 drive unit fit under the hood.

What’s more, the high-voltage charger, air conditioning compressor, thermal management module, and the water pump had to be relocated. Designers and engineers worked together to develop special holders, adapters, and mounting concepts to make it all work.

The ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept’s powertrain makes 362 horsepower and 406 pound-feet (550 Newton-meters) of torque, making it the most powerful electric Polo ever made. Compared to the road-going ID. Polo GTI, it makes 139 more horsepower and 192 more pound-feet of torque.

Yet, the car is still front-wheel drive. And if you’ve driven a relatively torquey EV with FWD, you know that transferring everything that an electric drive unit can give to the front wheels can prove difficult. But Volkswagen has that covered with an electronic front differential lock that uses a multiplate clutch. With it, the car can transfer power to both wheels if one of them starts to lose traction.

All of that power and torque give the electric track car a zero-to-62 miles per hour (0-100 kilometers per hour) sprint time of 4.7 seconds and a 149 miles pr hour (240 kilometers per hour) top speed. To enable this level of performance, the 52-kilowatt-hour battery, which is the same as in the production ID. Polo GTI, was tweaked to allow for a higher power output of up to 290 kW, as well as longer discharge periods at high outputs.

Hooked to a DC fast charger, the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept can take up to 105 kW, just like the regular ID. Polo GTI, which can go from 10% to 80% in 24 minutes.

The extra power and torque go hand in hand with plenty of changes to the body and underneath it. The one-off EV is 100 millimeters (3.9 inches) wider than the production model and sits 30 mm (1.1 in) lower than the standard ID. Polo. The same adaptive suspension as the production vehicle is used, but its setup is adjusted for track use.

The electric Clubsport Concept has just two doors instead of the regular ID. Polo’s four, and features a pretty aggressive body kit with wide wheel arches, functional air ducts, and a huge rear wing. GTI badges and red accents are everywhere, including in the interior, where the central touchscreen no longer acts as the infotainment center. In fact, the concept doesn’t have an infotainment system, as the central screen handles driving settings exclusively.

Bright red five-point harnesses protect the driver and front passenger sitting in Recaro racing bucket seats, while a red rollover bar has replaced the rear seats and cargo area.

The Volkswagen ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept is not yet intended for production, but the German automaker hasn’t ruled out the option entirely, saying that it has always associated the development of concept vehicles “with the theoretical option of turning a one-off into a new production derivative.”

The track-focused EV will make its first live appearance at the Essen Motor Show in Germany, which runs from November 27 through December 6.

#4453. Zenless Zone Zero's big end-of-year update brings multiplayer combat, free Zhao, and the first dual-form Agent

Zenless Zone Zero' is saying goodbye to 2025 with a bang, as update 2.5 gets fully revealed.

Zenless Zone Zero’s latest Special Program has delivered the good news on Version 2.5, To Be Fuel for the Night. This chapter is a big deal for a few reasons, not least of which because it brings an end to Season 2.

To start with, Version 2.5 arrives on December 30, making it the game’s last major update of the year, which also means players are in for some freebies to celebrate the new year.

Of course, the biggest addition in Version 2.5 is Ye Shunguang, the game’s new Agent, who’s a Void Hunter, and also Zenless Zone Zero’s first dual-form Agent. Zhao also becomes a playable Agent as part of this update - two things HoYoverse teased last week at The Game Awards.

Ye Shunguang’s unique attribute is Honed Edge, through which she can enter an Enlightened Mind state. Ye Shunguang’s signature Ether Veil can deliver Honed Edge damage as she applies a vulnerability effect to enemies. She arrives alongside her sidekick, Bangboo Sprout, who keeps with her swordplay theme by calling down flying swords.

Zhao is the other playable Agent as mentioned, an S-Rank Ice Defence legend. Zhao is a fast and nimble attacker who uses her giant greataxe to suppress enemies. Zhao can trigger Ether Veil: Wellspring by using Frostbite she accumulates, which buffs the entire squad.

Narratively, this particular chapter will reveal the fate of Waifei Peninsula. The quest is gonna take the squad deeper into the Lumite Mine ruins, and the new Perception Technique is how you’ll uncover the answers hidden within.

There’s a gameplay component to that, too. Ye Shunguang's Bladeflash Mirage ability will come in handy during the story’s big investigation, which comes with unique rewards, including a new W-Engine.

Version 2.5 is also the one set to give players the first taste of multiplayer combat thought he limited-time Joint Investigation: The Divine Maze event. As part of that, you can have three-Agent squads face off against each other in unique combat challenges.

There’s even more to get excited about in this one. Proxy Outpost lets you create your own Outposts, and join those created by other. This is more of a social feature than anything, though.

HoYoverse is also making a series of updates to Soldier 11, Grace, Soldier 0 – Anby, Ellen, and Burnice, all of whom will see their mechanics updated and their effectiveness boosted. #4452. BYD’s new Han EV spotted without camo, showing off its sleek fastback design

Who doesn’t love a good fastback? BYD’s new Han was spotted completely undisguised, giving us an early look at its sleek design and interior ahead of its expected debut next week.

After launching the flagship Great Han last month, or the “Da Han,” as it’s called in China, BYD is preparing to introduce another new member to the lineup.

BYD already sells the smaller Han, but the electric sedan is due for an overhaul. The new version appeared in a regulatory filing by China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) last month.

According to the filing, the next-generation BYD Han will be available in three battery electric (BEV) and one plug-in hybrid (PHEV) variants.

The Han EV will offer two single-motor rear-wheel-drive (RWD) options, with an output of 328 hp (245 kW) and 402 hp (300 kW). A dual-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) version will also be offered, delivering a combined 697 hp (520 kW).

All variants use BYD’s Blade LFP Battery and are expected to be equipped with its five-minute Flash Charging technology.

The PHEV version, on the other hand, uses a 1.5-liter engine and an electric motor with up to 268 hp (200 kW).

Ahead of its expected debut at the Guangzhou Auto Show on November 27, BYD’s new Han was captured in public without any disguise.

The images sent to Autohome show a design similar to the Great Han and other new Dynasty series vehicles, with its latest “Dragon Face” signature front-end look.

A few things have changed from the current model, including new headlights and a full-length light bar, while the Chinese symbol moved to the hood.

From the side, the Han features a sleek, fastback silhouette. The vehicle also features a roof-mounted LiDAR to support advanced driver-assistance features. The new Han is expected to feature BYD’s God’s Eye B ADAS system.

Inside, the new Han adopts BYD’s updated interior design. The new setup includes a floating center infotainment screen and a digital instrument panel behind a three-spoke steering wheel.

The center console is also updated with two wireless phone chargers and cupholders without covers.

Doesn't matter for us here in the USA (for now), but I wish the back was a little more sedan looking with a little more trunk lid. Otherwise, nice car.

BYD’s new Han is 5,156 mm long, 1,969 mm wide, and 1,507 mm tall, with a wheelbase of 3,030 mm, which is 161 mm longer than the current version.

The flagship Great Han is the largest of the series, measuring 5,256 mm long. After launching the Great Han on October 13, BYD sold 4,000 units by November 1.

Since the flagship sedan starts at 235,900 yuan, or about $35,000, the smaller Han will likely be closer to 200,000 yuan ($30,000) or less. The outgoing Han starts at 168,800 yuan ($25,000).

#4450. This Might Be The World's First Rivian R2 With A Two-Inch Lift, And It Looks Badass

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

The Rivian R2 may be a little tamer than its bigger brothers, the R1S and R1T, but that doesn’t mean that the aftermarket world can’t chime in and lend a helping hand. While the mid-size SUV carried over many of its larger siblings’ characteristics, it lacks one feature that could make the difference between getting back home the same day and spending hours trying to get unstuck: adjustable air suspension.

The R2 comes with fixed suspension, so the driver has to be very careful when choosing their lines, but thankfully, there are now a handful of companies out there that sell suspension lift kits for the R2.

Bullray Manufacturing made a custom lift kit for a Rivian R2 that’s used as a chase truck for the Off Grid racing team. The electric SUV, an R2 Performance, made an appearance at this year’s SEMA show in Las Vegas and was filmed by Out of Spec Bits.

The 2.0-inch metal lifters were fitted above the dampers, and the electric crossover retains its standard semi-active suspension. In other words, this is a body lift, not a suspension lift, but it shouldn’t matter too much, considering this is a unibody vehicle, after all. The high-voltage battery and electric motors are fitted directly to the underside of the body, so the added ground clearance should help protect vital components when going off the beaten track.

It’s also worth noting that EV Sportline, a company that specializes in aftermarket parts for electric vehicles, offers a 1.6-inch body lift kit for the Rivian R2.

Getting back to the green R2 that went to SEMA, it’s obvious that it’s fully kitted out for any overlanding experience. There’s a Baja Designs 40-inch light bar, a set of Maxtrax Extreme recovery boards, plenty of storage options on the roof, and a Rig’D tire carrier at the rear. A set of Yokohama Geolandar Mud-Terrain tires wrapped around 17-inch Method Racing wheels completes the look.

Inside, there’s a communications system, as well as a racing-spec GPS navigation system for the front passenger.

All in all, it looks really badass and shows that there’s a lot of potential in the aftermarket space for the Rivian R2. Clearly, the raised ride height and chunky tires will eat into the car’s official 330-mile range, but that’s to be expected.

#4449. Alpitronic’s new SC plant to build 400 kW and 1 MW fast chargers

Alpitronic, the company behind IONNA’s fast chargers, is investing nearly $34 million in a new South Carolina factory. It’ll build 400 kW DC fast chargers, plus a 1 megawatt (MW) system that can charge cars and heavy-duty trucks.

The $33.94 million project in Fort Mill is expected to create 70 jobs, the South Carolina Department of Commerce announced Wednesday. It’ll be the Bolzano, Italy-based Alpitronic’s first operation in South Carolina, just across the state line from its North American headquarters in Charlotte.

The HYC400 packs up to 400 kW into a single unit. If you’ve stopped at an IONNA Rechargery, you may have already plugged into one.

The HYC1000 works differently. A separate power cabinet can send up to 1 MW across as many as eight vehicles at once, shifting power between them as their charging needs change. Operators can configure it with CCS or NACS plugs for passenger EVs or a Megawatt Charging System (MCS) plug for compatible heavy-duty trucks.

Alpitronic’s 400 kW chargers were already being made in Wisconsin for Mercedes-Benz High-Power Charging in 2024. Alpitronic Americas CEO Patrik Herrnegger said the Fort Mill plant “will put US production under our direct control, bring us closer to our customers, and enable us to serve them more efficiently.”

The 173,315-square-foot site at 3560 Stateview Blvd. (pictured above) will also house a testing lab, repair operations, a warehouse, logistics space, and offices. South Carolina approved job development credits and awarded York County a $200,000 grant to help pay for building improvements.

The Ram Rampage will be aimed directly at Ford Maverick customers when it arrives in 2028.

These days, if you’re in the market for an affordable pickup, your options sort of start and end with the Ford Maverick. Or, at least they do if you’re looking to buy a new vehicle. That’s supposed to change in the near future, though. There’s the electric Slate pickup, and, at some point in 2028, Ram is scheduled to bring its compact Rampage to the United States.

In a recent interview with MoparInsiders, Ram’s new CEO, Matt VanDyke, took direct aim at the Ford Maverick. “Yeah, the value story is super important to many customers, and there hasn’t been enough choice,” VanDyke said. “And oh, by the way, we know exactly what Maverick is; it’s a nice product, and we think we can beat it.”

#4446. NSSL keeps growing its electric terminal truck fleet, with no plans to stop

After taking delivery of its first Orange EV e-Triever electric yard tractor in 2024, NSSL saw the electric light. The company has been moving quickly to transition its yard tractor fleet to zero emissions, and its efforts haven’t gone unnoticed: NSSL is now being recognized by the 2026 Canadian Clean Fleet Awards.

Toronto’s National Shunt Service, Ltd. (NSSL) added its first electric terminal truck to its trailer-moving operations back in 2024 – and they were impressed enough to quickly start buying more, putting their Orange e-Triever and Husk-e trucks to work at customers’ warehouses, distribution centers, and factories. The company has 42 electric trucks working at a number of sites in Canada (up from 27 in June), with plans to have 50 by the end of Q1 2027.

“(Electric is) part of every customer conversation we’re having today,” says Darren Fitzgerald, NSSL’s chief commercial officer. “If customers aren’t asking about electrification, we are bringing it to the conversation.”

The company’s commitment to decarbonization recently made them a 2026 Canadian Clean Fleets Award winner, recognizing their growing role in normalizing battery-electric, zero-emission commercial trucks across Canada.

NSSL used Geotab telematics to track pertinent data of each vehicle, giving what Fitzgerald called, “an essential overview of the entire fleet,” that enabled the company to compare efficiencies and cost, as well as the ability to plan ahead.

“The data allows us to identify potential maintenance issues before they result in an outage,” he explains. “Just as importantly, it gives us the analytics to understand idle time, fuel and energy consumption, utilization, and overall operating efficiency.”

If NSSL’s experience is anything like many, many, many others, they’ll find that the case for electrification is stronger than ever.

#4445. The Remnants Of The Electric Saab That Never Was Are Going Up For Auction

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

I don’t really know why, but I’ve always been fascinated by Saab, the ill-fated Swedish car manufacturer. Maybe it’s because it was always a little left-field, even when it was part of General Motors, or maybe I liked the cars’ design.

In any case, the Saab car brand has been dead for precisely a decade, but now an auction is selling off a unique piece of automotive history that has deep ties to the now-defunct marque.

The entire Emily GT project, which surfaced in 2023 after being developed in secrecy for half a decade, is being auctioned off in Sweden by Klaravik. The lot includes a working mule prototype, bodies, parts, accessories, drawings, and four complete Emily GT prototypes, which are billed as the only ones that will ever be available on the open market.

Developed by ex-Saab engineers who worked at NEVS, the company that picked up the pieces after the storied automaker’s bankruptcy in 2012, the Emily GT was envisioned as a next-generation electric model with four in-wheel motors and a driving range of up to 600 miles, courtesy of a high-voltage battery that could, in theory, top out at 175 kilowatt-hours. According to technical drawings obtained by SaabPlanet, the standard-range car would have had a 105-kWh pack, while the mid-spec model was designed for a 140-kWh pack.

Wireless charging at up to 11 kW was also in the cards, and no fewer than four body styles, including a shooting brake, a sporty sedan, a two-door coupe, and a cabriolet.

The four electric motors, developing a combined 490 horsepower, enabled a quite sophisticated torque vectoring system, leading to great road manners. However, none of it materialized. NEVS never had the cash to move forward with the project, and now all of the pieces are being sold off.

“For us, this is a historic event, and I believe many Saab fans feel the same way,” said Nina Selander, CEO of NEVS. “Despite only ever being built as a handful of prototypes, the Emily GT has achieved iconic status. That says a lot about the fascination with the car. By making the sale available in this way, we hope to attract car enthusiasts all over the world whose hearts beat for Saab.”

For the right buyer, it’s the perfect starter kit for a new car company, but it won’t come cheap. According to the Swedish local newspaper Ttela, the starting bid will be roughly $1.5 million (15 million SEK), and the auction house is not splitting the lot’s components into individual pieces. Everything is bundled into a single lot, so whoever has the highest bid goes home with everything.

Separately, Klaravik is auctioning off the world’s only NEVS Sango, a prototype of a self-driving vehicle designed for public transport that never materialized.

Both online auctions will go live on November 25 and will run through December 9.

#4443. GM’s V2G pilot wants to pay California drivers for power from parked EVs

GM Energy and WeaveGrid are launching a vehicle-to-grid (V2G) pilot that will let select Southern California Edison (SCE) customers send electricity from their EV batteries back to the grid. Eligible drivers could get more than $16,000 in help with equipment and installation, and earn money when the grid needs their power.

GM says the pilot participants will be its first EV drivers in California to export power from their cars to their homes. Through the California Energy Commission, eligible customers in SCE’s Emergency Load Reduction Program can get up to $8,000 toward a GM Energy V2H system and up to $8,099 toward eligible installation costs, including connecting the system to the grid.

Chevy, GMC, and Cadillac EV drivers can use time-of-use energy management to take advantage of lower rates and may be paid for participating in eligible demand-response events. How much they save or earn depends on their rate plan, electricity use, and participation.

GM already offers managed charging through 13 utilities, and each program varies by utility.

An EV battery stores direct current (DC), and your house and the grid use alternating current (AC). GM’s current home backup system uses a wall-mounted inverter to convert the power. With AC bidirectional charging, the car’s onboard inverter does the job. Moving that work into the car could make the equipment on your garage wall simpler and cheaper to install.

Not in CA, but we use solar, time of use, and EVs to minimize our energy costs. We’re not feeding power back to the grid from our cars, but the combo of TOU, solar and EVs does allow us to reduce costs significantly. Solar covers all the expensive peak power, I have the cars start charging early enough to use any extra solar, and the rest is off peak at half cost.

GM is joining CharIN‘s North American AC V2G task force, which is working to align technical standards, equipment certification, and utility approval requirements. In Southern California, the pilot will give GM and its partners a look at how the process works for drivers, from signing up and getting the hardware installed to getting utility approval and sending power back.

#4442. Retromobile Vintage-Car Expo Comes to NYC

A newcomer from Paris muscles its way onto America’s collector-car calendar.

Retromobile is a classic-car event in Paris that dates back to 1976. This year, CEO Gérard Neveu brings it to New York City for the first time, in what is planned to be an annual event. Like the Paris original, Retromobile NYC takes place indoors (at the Jacob Javits Center). It’s not a concours, although there are some Pebble Beach–worthy vehicles on display. It’s more commerce focused, with a major auction (Gooding Christie’s) taking place.

Other auction houses, including Mecum and Bring a Trailer, also have a presence, and several high-end classic-car dealers have set up shop as well. Additionally, there’s a whole ecosystem of supporting vendors, from automobilia to wearables to insurance to watches. Art also features prominently. A significant display of art cars, in its own museum-like space, is curated by CART Department. There are also works for sale by current automotive artists. In all, there are roughly 100 exhibitors.

#4441. Hyundai’s N Vision 74 Was One Of The Coolest Car Designs In Recent Memory. Now It's Shelved

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Hyundai absolutely knocked the teasers for then Hyundai N Vision 74 out of the park. I mean, a hydrogen-electric hybrid that's an actual sports car, with all the style of a 1970s wedge car? The internet loved the idea. But, unfortunately, that's probably what the N Vision will remain—an idea. The plans for production are on ice.

Simon Loasby, the head of Hyundai's Design Center, explained toThe Drive that the decision came down to business. When the South Korean automaker simply couldn't justify the business case for the car, it decided to not move forward with production in the foreseeable future. Here's what Loasby told the publication when asked if the automaker planned to make a production version of the N Vision 74:

At the moment, no. We were really on it. We had the production clay model of it and the exterior, interior, and so on.

It comes down to the maths of how you judge what the business case is. And that if you’re very tight with the business case on only that car, the volumes of that car and the impact, you got no chance.

If you open it to the overall brand-raising profile value of that, you have a bigger chance. But as yet, [no].

Many of you reading this are likely part car lover and part EV enthusiast. Me too, which is why I'm immensely disappointed that Hyundai decided to cancel plans to build this awesome concept.

After all, EVs are damn fun. Instant torque, low center of gravity. It's pretty much everything that an an enthusiast wants out of a sports car—even if EVs inherently are a bit heavier and lack a row-your-own gearbox. It also used the beloved Stinger as a base to build the car. But rather than the 3.3-liter twin-turbocharged V6, Hyundai stuffed it with the Nexo's hydrogen fuel cells and two electric motors.

One of the coolest parts of the coupe was its retro styling. That was inspired by the original Hyundai Pony coupe, which was designed by the legendary Giorgetto Giugiaro (the same guy who designed the VW Golf, DeLorean DMC-12, and a plethora of other icons).

Loasby says that Hyundai's head of design, SangYup Lee, convinced the company not to throw away the design work from the N Vision concept. Instead, it reused some of the design elements for new models like the all new 2027 Hyundai Elantra.

"[T]hat top view as you notice, even in the pillar and side view up to the roof crease and the flatness of the roof, that’s all playbook N74," he told The Drive. He later hinted more could be coming: “Just imagine what an N version of [Elantra] can be. It’s really good, it’s awesome.”

Maybe it was the idea of using hydrogen that killed the N Vision concept. Or perhaps that coupes have seem to go the way of the dodo in recent years. Whatever the reason, it's just unfortunate for enthusiasts who were pumped to see a sport-tuned FCEV in the distance.

One glimmer of hope is that Loasby didn't say that the car is dead forever. Just that Hyundai couldn't make a business case for it "at the moment." Perhaps we might get something with two-doors, a striking design, and battery power in the future. Until then, I'm staying pumped about the Rivian R3X.

#4440. Double guns: ultra-class haul truck packs dual-gun MCS charging, 4 MWh battery

NHL may not be a household name, but its all-new, all-electric NTE240E ultra-class haul track could change that with a 240 ton payload, over 4.1 MWh of battery, advanced regenerative braking, and a world’s first double-gun MCS charging setup.

For the uninitiated, Inner Mongolia North Hauler Joint Stock Co., Ltd. (NHL) is a Chinese heavy equipment manufacturer specializing in the enormous rigid-frame haul trucks used in open-pit mining operations. Established in 1988, NHL has decades of experience building mining trucks for customers around the world, including some of the industry’s largest diesel-electric hybrids. The brand’s new NTE240E is different, representing a company’s real push into battery-electric mining equipment, and it’s powering that push with some seriously ambitious technology.

Let’s start with the battery. The NTE240E packs an absolutely MASSIVE battery pack, with the highest-capacity versions offering up to 4,100 kWh (4.1 MWh) of onboard energy storage. Keeping that much battery topped off is no small task, which is why NHL developed an equally ambitious energy replenishment strategy supporting dual-gun MCS charging, allowing its town-sized battery to go from 20% to 90% in under an hour.

That means operators can take advantage of shift changes and scheduled rest breaks to top off the battery without sacrificing an entire work shift to charging – but even more impressive than the fact that all that juice can be crammed into so big a battery in so little time is the fact that, according to NHL, it can be done at just 25°C (about 77°F).

Plugging in isn’t the only way the NTE240E drinks its juice. NHL’s new dynamic power reception system uses overhead current collectors to supply electricity directly to the truck while it’s climbing loaded mine roads, allowing it to then “ride the brakes” for more energy all the way downhill.

The combined technologies allow NHL’s operators to keep the massive trucks moving without relying entirely on their onboard batteries. The result is a claimed 15% improvement in energy efficiency over the ultra-class industry average.

That efficiency turns into savings, which means the economics of running an NTE240E could be just as compelling as the emissions savings – and those are substantial. NHL says each NTE240E can reduce harmful carbon emissions by more than 2,000 tons annually, even as it cuts operating costs by more than 60% compared to a comparably capable diesel.

What’s more, because the big BEV’s electrical system eliminates the need for engine-related hardware like generators and the maintenance and overhaul costs associated with those components. Taken as a whole, the NHL seems to be a compelling offering … but that’s not for me to say. You guys are the experts – let us know what you think of the new NHL NTE240E, in the comments.

#4439. Legendary game creator Vince Zampella has passed away

Vince Zampella, co-creator of Call of Duty, and a veteran studio head responsible for some of the biggest franchises in the world, is gone.

Vince Zampella, known for co-creating the Call of Duty series, among many other roles, has died. Zampella, 55, died in a car crash in Los Angeles on Sunday. The fatal crash killed him, along with the occupant of his car.

According to NBC, Zampella’s Ferrari hit a concrete barrier after leaving a tunnel in the San Gabriel Mountains, north of Los Angeles. Zampella was unfortunately trapped in an ensuing car fire, and the passenger was ejected.

Vince Zampella is one of the industry’s most prolific creators. His storied career is long, and is responsible for some of the biggest shooter franchises in history. It started with Medal of Honor in the 90s, a game that changed WW2 shooters forever.

Zampella later co-founded the legendary Infinity Ward in 2002, the team that would go on to redefine multiplayer shooters forever. Infinity Ward is the studio responsible for the Call of Duty series, which remains one of the biggest games for publisher Activision, and the entire industry.

Zampella then left the studio he founded in 2010 following a major fallout with Activision. He, along with longtime collaborator, Jason West, went to rival publisher EA to form Respawn Entertainment.

Respawn went on to create the Titanfall series, and later Apex Legends. The studio is responsible for non-shooters, of course, like the third-person action game series Star Wars Jedi. Zampella was instrumental in making the game possible, having hired God of War 3 director Stig Asmussen to helm a team within Respawn out of a desire to diversify the studio’s output and prove he can do more than make shooters.

Zampella had only recently met with journalists and peers at The Game Awards, where Battlefield 6 was nominated for multiple awards. Battlefield 6 is the most successful game in series history, in part as a result of Zampella’s leadership. The legendary leader was given the reigns of the struggling multiplayer shooter franchise in 2021, with a goal of finding a viable future.

Zampella’s sudden death has shaken the industry, and many mourn his loss as the news started spreading.

“We are heartbroken by the loss of Vince Zampella, a creative leader whose work shaped generations of players and helped define what modern shooters and action games could be,” EA said in a statement.

“While his impact reached far beyond any one game or studio, we will remember Vince for how he showed up every day, trusting his teams, encouraging bold ideas, and believing in Battlefield and the people building it. We are deeply grateful for his leadership, his generosity, and the care he brought to everything he touched, and we will carry that forward with us.”

#4438. 2027 Volkswagen Golf GTI Rabbit Edition Changes More Than Looks

It’s a very special heritage model but, sadly, VW doesn’t give customers the one thing we’d all want out of a new GTI: There’s still no manual.

Do you ever find yourself yearning for the feeling you got the first time you drove the Mk 1 Volkswagen Rabbit? The diminutive VW helped usher the hot-hatch segment into the United States. Volkswagen can’t very well sell you a Mk 1 Rabbit any longer, so instead, the company unveiled a limited-production Rabbit Edition for the 2027 Golf GTI lineup.

Specifically, the Rabbit Edition is arriving for the 2027-½ model year as a sort of midyear update to the GTI lineup. The special edition will slot between the S and the SE in the GTI’s roster and will come with a handful of performance upgrades generally limited to the Autobahn trim. The Rabbit version adds DCC adaptive damping, rides on 19-inch wheels, and wears a set of summer tires, rather than the all-season tires that generally come with the S.

See all results for new 2027 Volkswagen Golf GTI for sale near 29414

As far as cosmetic changes go, the special edition opts for a blacked-out logo design over the Dark Moss Green Metallic paint, which includes a set of front and rear badges that VW pulled from the Golf R Black Edition’s parts bin. The logos are joined by a black grille, black headlight elements (which are typically red), black wheels, black mirror caps, and a black roof. The one badge that isn’t black is the chrome Rabbit badge on the rear, which serves as an homage to the original.

The Rabbit Edition will be limited to the United States when it goes on sale in the second quarter of next year. Exact pricing hasn’t been announced, but the Rabbit should cost somewhere between the $36,230 starting price of the S and the $40,420 starting price of the SE.

#4437. BYD's Latest SUV Can Hide Its Steering Wheel When You Don't Need It

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

I have to admit that when I first saw the Fangchengbao Tai 9 stow its steering wheel away on social media, I assumed that it was AI. It wasn't. This BYD brand's new SUV can indeed retract its steering wheel right into the dashboard. However, it’s not quite used for the reason you’d think.

The Tai 9 is a six-seat, plug-in hybrid SUV about the same size as the Cadillac Escalade IQ, and it sits at the top of the Fangchengbao range. BYD’s Chinese-market brand and naming structure can be confusing, but in essence, Fangchengbao is one of BYD's premium brands.

Power comes from two electric motors that produce 536 horsepower at peak, while a 1.5-liter turbocharged engine is responsible for any combustion-powered driving. The Tai 9 has a 66.5 kWh battery that is capable of BYD’s flash charging technology. The brand claims it can sprint from 10% to 97% in nine minutes.

Those are all very compelling specs, but the most interesting part of the Tai 9 is the top-of-the-line Foldable Smart Cabin trim. Since the Tai 9 uses a steer-by-wire system, the steering wheel can fold up and stow itself in the dashboard. BYD says that takes about 10 seconds.

However, this isn’t for any sort of autonomous driving. China’s autonomous driving rules are strict, and no automaker in the country has approval for commercially sold eyes-off, hands-off driver assist features. Instead, the folding steering wheel is primarily for comfort and space, specifically when the car is stationary. Photos of the feature in action show that stowing away the steering wheel makes extra room for a little table setup.

This isn’t entirely unprecedented. The new trend in China is for large SUVs to be third spaces where buyers can comfortably hang out, even when they aren't driving. The Tai 9’s Nappa leather, comfy seats, and second-row folding screen are meant to make it a calming, relaxing space to spend time. It's similar in concept to what we’ve seen on the Zeekr Mix and SkyNomad N90 Studio.

Still, despite the Tai 9’s folding steering wheel not being for self-driving, I wouldn’t be surprised if it does show up in cars for that reason someday, as manufacturers strive to make cars that can truly drive themselves.

A car with no steering wheel at all might feel risky and uncomfortable to some car buyers, especially if it's like Tesla’s Cybercab, which can’t be driven manually at all above low speeds. Yet, if there were a backup to take control, I could see that putting some minds at ease.

The Fangchengbao Tai 9 is on sale in China for about $42,000. The top-of-the-line model with the foldable steering wheel is about $49,500.

#4435. 2027 Toyota Sienna Drive: More than Meets the Eye

The Toyota Sienna doesn’t look any different, but big changes to its hybrid powertrain promise more efficiency and more power.

Most mid-cycle refreshes touch only the surface stuff: a new grille, new headlights, new wheel designs. They typically don’t venture too far into the mechanicals. Toyota flipped the script in its approach to the 2027 Sienna hybrid minivan, mostly leaving the visuals alone and focusing instead on the substantive bits. The result is a minivan that’s more upgraded than it looks.

Much like a person who is very bad at seeing those magic-eye illusions, you could stare at a picture of the 2027 Sienna all day and nothing new would make itself apparent. The exterior is unchanged, although one paint color (Cypress) has been dropped in favor of a new hue (Storm Cloud). The trims have also been rejiggered: The Limited is gone, and the XSE picks up some of its features and becomes the new penultimate trim beneath Platinum. Otherwise, every inch of mid-cycle-refresh effort went into the underlying tech and the powertrain.

See all results for used cars for sale near 97229

The base LE loses its 8.0-inch infotainment screen as Toyota democratizes digital real estate, granting every Sienna a 12.3-inch infotainment screen and a 12.3-inch gauge display. New LED cabin lighting arrives, and the rear-seat entertainment picks up major upgrades with native apps and a new touchscreen. The sound-deadening material behind the dashboard has also been tweaked.

We saved the best bits for last. The 2027 Sienna adopts Toyota’s latest (sixth-gen) hybrid powertrain, which first arrived in the Lexus ES. The old nickel-metal hydride battery is replaced by a lithium-ion pack that stores more energy, and it feeds a redesigned and more efficient electric motor to produce a combined 251 horsepower—six more than its predecessor. All-wheel-drive models energize the rear axle with an additional motor, though that doesn’t raise output any. Toyota estimates a 7.5-second run to 60 mph in front-wheel-drive guise, rising to 7.6 with all-wheel drive (since there’s more mass and no extra oomph). Either way, that’s 0.3 to 0.4 second quicker than the 2026 Sienna. Our long-term 2021 Toyota Sienna Limited AWD did the deed in 7.6 seconds.

The 2026 Sienna earned EPA fuel-economy estimates of 36 city, 36 highway, and 36 combined for front-wheel-drive models and 35/36/35 for all-wheel-drive variants. While official numbers have not yet been released for the 2027 model, Toyota claims city improvements of 3 mpg (FWD) and 4 mpg (AWD), with combined estimates rising between 1 and 2 mpg.

Because these changes might not seem like much on paper, Toyota gave us access to both a 2026 Sienna and a 2027 Sienna to better experience the changes. And we’re glad we had that opportunity, because the revised Sienna does make for a vastly improved driving experience.

See all results for used cars for sale near 97229

We liked the 2027 Sienna more before we even pushed the start button. The Sienna’s new steering wheel puts switches in more sensible locations; it’s much easier to operate on the fly, plus it looks better. The 2026 model’s tech feels a full step behind the 2027 model’s, with its analog gauge cluster (on the lower trims) and tiny info display, or the complete lack of USB-C ports. Thankfully, with the 2027 Sienna’s new tech comes a whole host of electrical-system changes, including a move to USB-C. Our tangled morass of a cable drawer thanks you, Toyota.

In addition to sprinkling better ports around the cabin, the Sienna’s new updated tech also enhances the driving experience. The electronic power steering is lighter at lower road speeds, making around-town navigation slightly less onerous, and it also exhibits better on-center stability at highway speeds, again eliminating some tedium. The brakes also include a feature Toyota calls Vehicle Braking Posture Control, which applies braking to individual wheels to reduce body roll in cornering; after taking both Siennas to our 10Best evaluation loop, we can confirm that the revised Sienna does corner ever so slightly flatter, and you don’t even need to drive like a Car and Driver editor to feel the improvement.

As for the Sienna’s powertrain, we loved it in the latest generation of Lexus ES, and we very much enjoy it here as well. As Toyota promised, the sixth-gen hybrid brings noticeable improvements to noise, vibration, and harshness. In the 2026 model, the combustion engine sounds and feels coarser low in the rev range. In the 2027 model, the powertrain is both smoother and quieter, with an audible reduction in cabin noise (a change we’re excited to get the chance to confirm via testing at a later date). Simply put, driving the 2027 Sienna offers a more serene experience—for both driver and passengers—than you’d find in its predecessor.

Some changes incur massive cost penalties, but the 2027 Sienna doesn't ask too much extra off the top. It's estimated to come in around $44,500 for the base LE model with front-wheel drive. For context, the 2026 Sienna started at $42,915 for the base LE, rising to $60,305 for the top-spec Platinum; the slightly more rugged Woodland Edition was $53,695. Given just how much better the 2027 Sienna drives, we think it’s worth the higher cost of entry.

#4434. Love and Deepspace 5.0 update brings together all five love interests for the first time

Love and Deepspace is getting a big update to celebrate its second anniversary, and there's a lot to dig through.

If you can believe it, Love and Deepspace is almost two-years-old, and Infold Games is celebrating the moment in a few major ways. The Throne of Eros update brings the game up to version 5.0, and it’s one for fans of all love interests.

For one, this is the first time all five of them are brought together. The update is also adding some important new features, alongside anniversary events, and more.

Throne of Eros also doubles as the new Wish Pool, which is the one that has all of the game’s love interests in a single banner. This is a limited-time affair, of course, but it’s not the only thing you should look forward to here.

There’s also the Memory Growth Bonus, another limited-time event that you can take advantage of to grow your Memories. The even bigger news is that you can target your Wishes through the Xspace Echo, which lets you select five Memories to create your own pool from. You can use this to get any Memories you might not have, of course.

On the topic of Memories, you’ll also be able to unlock new second anniversary KV Memories, as part of a Yearly Highlights Event that will let you look back on your own journey with the game over the past year.

On the story and narrative side, Throne of Eros adds two new main stories, with new branches for Xavier, and Rafayel. There’s even a narrative-specific event that will run throughout the anniversary period, through which you can earn two daily outfits for each of the five love interests.

The celebrations also extend to new anniversary content like mail, and video calls. You can purchase a Yearly Pass, and check out some new arrivals at the Lunar Shop.

Beyond the anniversary content, version 5.0 also adds a new feature to the game: Home, which essentially offers a hub to get you directly to interacting with love interests that doesn’t have to do with combat or story.

You can also expect various other quality of life updates that touch on the Journal, Phone Moments Search, Resources Quick Cleanup, and new Tete-a-Tete that should make interacting with all of them more streamlined.

While this is a special banner, you should brush up on how banners work in Love and Deepspace if you’re unfamiliar. As always, it’s never not a good idea to check our Love and Deepspace codes page for some freebies.

#4433. Volkswagen’s new ID. Polo GTI Clubsport is the electric hot hatch we want, but can’t have

Volkswagen revealed the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept, an electric pocket rocket with a massive rear wing and 362 horsepower.

We knew Volkswagen was cooking something “really spicy” up after teasing the new GTI hot hatch earlier this week.

Volkswagen launched the first-generation Golf GTI in 1976, which essentially defined the hot hatch. To celebrate the brand’s legendary performance badge, a signature of its sporty, practical hatchbacks, VW is entering a new era with its first fully electric GTI.

The GTI has been “one of Volkswagen’s great success stories for 50 years,” Volkswagen’s technical development boss, Kai Grünitz, said.

After opening pre-orders for the ID. Polo GTI last month, the brand’s first EV to wear the badge, Volkswagen introduced the Clubsport Concept, a souped-up two-door electric pocket rocket.

The new ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept shows “how much more potential there is in the electric GTI world,” according to Grünitz.

It’s based on the production ID. Polo GTI uses the same MEB+ platform, but VW reengineered it with a larger electric motor to pump out more power.

The Clubsport is powered by a 362 hp (270 kW) front-mounted electric motor (APP550) that’s typically used in the rear of VW’s larger EVs, like the ID. Tiguan and the ID.7. That’s up considerably from the 233 hp (166 kW) and 213 lb-ft of torque of the standard ID. Polo GTI offers.

Thomas Schmall, CEO of Volkswagen Group Components, said the APP550 motor is “one of the most efficient electric drives in its class.”

Thanks to an electronically controlled front differential lock (VAQ), Volkswagen said, the Clubsport version can sprint from 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 km/h) in 4.7 seconds, beating the standard ID. Polo GTI by a full two seconds (6.8 seconds).

Volkswagen also fine-tuned the adaptive chassis control (DCC) to make it racetrack-ready and added new ceramic brakes to help slow it down.

The Clubsport version uses the same 52 kW NMC battery as the ID. Polo GTI, which can provide up to 389 hp (290 kW), Volkswagen said, enabling a top speed of 149 mph (240 km/h).

On the exterior, the Clubsport is a two-door model rather than a four-door. It’s 100 mm longer than the standard ID. Polo GTI, with each wing flared an additional 50 mm. It also gets a large motorsport splitter up front, a wider rear end, a new diffuser, and a massive carbon-fiber rear wing.

Inside, the cabin is tailored to the racetrack with a minimalist, stripped-down, two-seater layout. As such, there’s no infotainment system, just a center display to switch between drive modes.

The dash panel, side trims, and other interior elements feature dark ArtVelours microfibre with red topstitching, reinforcing the racetrack-ready interior.

Following the ID. Polo GTI, new ID.3 GTI, and Golf GTI Edition 50, the new ID. Polo Clubsport is the fourth model to debut this year under the performance badge.

Volkswagen opened pre-orders for the ID. Polo GTI last month, starting at 39,995 euros (about $45,000). In early 2027, Volkswagen will open orders for the ID.3 GTI, the second EV to wear the badge, and its first rear-wheel-drive (RWD) GTI.

And American compact car enthusiasts drool over more unobtanium.

The company will showcase the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport concept car at the Essen Motor Show next week, starting on November 27.

Volkswagen didn’t confirm plans to launch a production version, but don’t expect it to reach the States.

The standard VW ID. Polo and GTI are not sold in the US, so the souped-up Clubsport variant likely won’t be either. Hopefully, VW changes its mind and proves us wrong.

#4431. Genshin Impact Version Luna 4 introduces three new playable characters, including the long-awaited Moon Maiden Columbina

The first major Genshin Impact update in 2026 is almost here, bringing characters we've been waiting a while to play, and more besides.

Genshin Impact’s latest Special Program has spilled all the beans on the game’s next major update, Luna 4. The update, which arrives on January 14, kicks off 2026 with several bits of new content, including some previously-teased characters.

Dubbed Traveler on a Winter's Night, Luna 4 introduces three new playable characters, and brings back The Lantern Rite event to celebrate the beginning of the new year.

The first new arrival in Version Luna 4 is Columbina Hyposelenia, the Moon Maiden. Columbina is a 5-Star Hydro Catalyst wielder. Her kit revolves around supporting the squad via Lunar Reactions. She can trigger coordinated Lunar Reaction DMG, even when she’s off the field.

The Moon Maiden’s special ability, Lunar Domain, further boosts all Lunar Reactions by applying a DMG bonus, including summoning more thundercloud strikes for Lunar-Charged reactions. Columbina is also capable of converting Electro-Charged, Bloom, and Hydro Crystallize reactions into Lunar Reactions, as well as revive fallen squad members.

Speaking of elemental reactions, new in this version is Lunar-Crystallize, a new reaction that’s triggered when Geo meets Hydro (under certain conditions). When triggered, Lunar-Crystallize summons three Moondrifts near enemies. When triggered three times, Moondrift Harmony gets activated, dealing Geo DMG to enemies caught in its radius.

Then there’s Zibai, an Adeptus from Liyue. Zibai is another 5-Star character, a Geo Sword wielder. Zibai can, through entering a special state where they can build up energy, unleash an Elemental Skill that deals Lunar-Crystallize DMG.

The longer the fight goes on, the more Lunar-Crystallize reactions are triggered, the higher (and more often) the damage of Zibai’s Elemental Skill becomes.

Luna 4 continues the Nod-Krai story arc, with a big confrontation with Il Dottore. This is the focus of the new Archon Quest, completing which will earn you a new outfit. There’s a gameplay element to that new chapter, too, with the reveal of Piramida, a new area north of the region. Piramida is the headquarters of the Lightkeepers.

The first phase of Luna 4’s Event Wishes will, unsurprisingly, feature Columbina. It’ll also include reruns of Ineffa. The second phase is when Zibai becomes available, alongside another newcomer: Illuga, a 4-Star, polearm-wielding Geo Lightkeeper. The second phase’s rerun will be Neuvillette, who’s also going to have a new outfit in the shop at a discount.

Version Luna 4 brings back the annual Lantern Rite event, taking place in the mainland of Liyue. The event features its own set of minigames with unique rewards, alongside new stories of the Adepti.

All around Liyue Harbor, you’ll be able to place Xiao Lanterns and inscribe them with messages for others to read. You’ll also earn some Fortune Coins from Auspicious Treasure Trees, which you can later exchange for gifts.

All players will receive 1,600 Primogems through the in-game mail. If you log in regularly, you can earn up to ten Intertwined Fates. Lantern Rite has a new outfit for Yaoyao, which is also where you have a chance to earn one 4-Star Liyue character for free.

Finally, you can look forward to the new Classic Mode in Miliastra Wonderland, which lets you invite select Teyvat characters to join you.

#4430. Tesla FSD approved in Italy, the first big EU market to say yes

Italy’s transport ministry has granted provisional approval to Tesla Assisted Driving, the name Tesla now uses for “Full Self-Driving (Supervised)” in Europe. Italy becomes the 12th European country to allow the system, and the first of the EU’s big markets.

It also didn’t wait for Brussels. The EU committee that decides on bloc-wide recognition isn’t expected to vote until December at the earliest.

Deputy Prime Minister and Transport Minister Matteo Salvini announced the decision on X on Friday. He wrote that the ministry (MIT) gave the green light after a “thorough technical feasibility check,” and that Italy is getting ahead of the EU recognition process, which he described as “still being defined.”

Tesla Europe followed with a one-liner, “Now approved in Italy, rollout begins soon,” and a video of one of its cars driving itself through Rome. There’s no firm rollout date yet.

It’s still a Level 2 driver-assist system. It can steer, brake, accelerate, and handle intersections and lane changes, but the driver has to supervise at all times and stays fully responsible for the car.

The Dutch vehicle authority RDW was first, approving FSD Supervised on April 10 under Article 39 of the EU type-approval regulation. Other member states can then recognize that approval nationally, one by one.

Ten did before Italy: Belgium, Croatia, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Latvia, Lithuania, Slovakia, and Slovenia. Those are mostly small markets. Together with the Netherlands, they add up to about 70 million people, or roughly 15% of the EU’s population.

Italy alone has about 59 million people, so Friday’s decision nearly doubles the share of Europeans who can legally use the system, to close to 30%.

Rome’s position moved fast. In April, Senator Carlo Calenda formally asked Salvini’s ministry to prioritize the approval. On October 29, Salvini posted that he’d had a “very positive and constructive” call with Elon Musk and that Italy supported a “swift EU approval,” which read at the time as backing for an EU-level decision, not a national one. Three weeks later, Italy went national.

A lot changed in between. Tesla dropped the “Full Self-Driving” name in Europe after Germany’s Transport Ministry called it misleading, and cut the maximum speed margin from 50% to 10% over the limit. Then on November 16, the RDW approved stricter driver monitoring, including hands on the wheel above 130 km/h. That’s the version Italy is approving.

The EU’s Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles (TCMV) pushed the Tesla vote to December after holding only discussions in October. Bloc-wide approval needs a qualified majority: at least 15 of 27 member states, representing at least 65% of the EU population.

Germany said in October it would back approval after Tesla agreed to the rename and the speed cap. If it follows through, Germany and the 12 approving countries would cover roughly 47% of the EU’s population.

That’s progress for Tesla, but it’s not 65%. France refused a national approval in July, and Spain hasn’t recognized the Dutch approval. Tesla needs at least one of them, plus most of the remaining holdouts.

I haven't driven a car in Rome or Milan for quite some time but this sounds like a spicey recipe for disaster.

This is a real win for Tesla, and for Italian owners with HW4 cars who have been paying for a feature they couldn’t use at home. Italy is Tesla’s first big European market to say yes, and it shifts momentum going into December.

But it’s pretty crazy that now Europe is going to get a safer FSD than in the US.

I bet that this will get reflected in the data, if we ever get to see it.
